headline: Samsung confirms Galaxy Watch 9 will be an AI-powered health companion with new features
summary: Samsung Health's major upgrade will transform the upcoming Galaxy Watch into a proactive, intelligent health partner, introducing features like an AI-powered Energy Score and adaptive Daily Cardio Load.
details: Samsung has officially teased the upcoming Galaxy Watch 9 as an "AI-powered health companion." This confirmation comes directly from the brand, highlighting a significant upgrade to its Samsung Health platform.

The enhanced Samsung Health is set to transform the new Galaxy Watch series into a "proactive, intelligent health partner." While specific hardware details remain under wraps, leaks suggest there will be three models: the Watch 9, Watch 9 Classic, and a premium Watch Ultra 2, with the latter potentially offering 5G connectivity.

At the core of these new capabilities is a "truly AI-powered health platform" within Samsung Health. This includes a new AI-driven "Energy Score," which aggregates data from five key pillars: Sleep, Activity, Nutrition, Mindfulness, and Vitals, providing a comprehensive overview of the user's well-being.

The Energy Score will offer personalized health tips based on these metrics. This feature is expected to be a central part of the Galaxy Watch 9's user interface, making it easily accessible and integral to the user experience, similar to how Apple Watch utilizes its Activity Rings.

For more advanced fitness tracking, a new "Daily Cardio Load" feature will provide nuanced suggestions by considering "accumulated cardiovascular strain" and other fitness details. Unlike previous tools, it can adapt recommendations and suggest rest times based on temporary factors like fatigue or energy levels.

Another announced tool, "Fitness Index," is designed to inform and optimize exercise routines. These new AI-powered features aim to provide a more personalized and adaptive health monitoring experience for users.

headline_marked: Microsoft [[Considers Spinning Off Xbox]] Amidst Major Restructuring
headline: Microsoft Considers Spinning Off Xbox Amidst Major Restructuring
summary: New Xbox CEO Asha Sharma is reportedly exploring options from subsidiaries to outright sales as the company reevaluates its gaming division's future.
details: Microsoft is reportedly preparing for significant layoffs within its Xbox division and is reevaluating plans for its next-generation Project Helix console.

According to a new report from The Information, Microsoft has considered dramatic measures to make its Xbox unit more sustainable, including turning it into a wholly owned subsidiary, a joint venture, or spinning it off entirely.
While nothing is said to be imminent, new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella are apparently not ruling out any options for the future of Xbox.
Sharma has secured approval to invest heavily in tentpole titles like Halo and Fallout, with major upcoming releases Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution slated to be Xbox exclusives.
This investment in popular franchises is likely to come at the expense of smaller studios and games that have not met sales expectations.
caption:
Microsoft hasn't ruled out spinning off its Xbox division as it reportedly prepares for major layoffs and reevaluates its gaming strategy.

Microsoft is reportedly preparing for significant layoffs within its Xbox division and is reevaluating plans for its next-generation Project Helix console.

While nothing is said to be imminent, new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella are apparently not ruling out any options for the future of Xbox.

Sharma has secured approval to invest heavily in tentpole titles like Halo and Fallout, with major upcoming releases Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution slated to be Xbox exclusives.

This investment in popular franchises is likely to come at the expense of smaller studios and games that have not met sales expectations.
